title: Strong wind advisory issued for several areas - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre has issued a strong wind advisory for the Northern and North-central provinces, as well as Hambantota and Trincomalee districts, effective until 11.00 a.m. tomorrow (23).

According to the advisory issued at 11.00 a.m. today (22), strong winds reaching speeds of 40–50 kmph could occur at times in these areas due to active south-west monsoon conditions.

The Department of Meteorology warned that the strong winds could damage roof tiles and sheets, power and communication lines, and may result in the breaking of tree branches and uprooting of large trees.

It also cautioned that paddy crops, banana and papaya trees, orchards, harbour yachts, and low-lying coastal areas could be affected, with a possibility of seawater inundation near the coast.

The public has been advised to remain cautious of damaged roofs, fallen trees and power lines, and to stay alert to changing weather conditions.

People requiring emergency assistance have been requested to contact local disaster management authorities and follow future weather advisories issued by the Department of Meteorology.

title: DAPH calls for coordinated plan to eliminate rabies by 2030 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Department of Animal Production and Health (DAPH) has called for a planned and humane approach to eliminate rabies in Sri Lanka by 2030, highlighting the need for cooperation among government institutions, veterinarians, local authorities and animal welfare organisations.

A senior official of the Department said that achieving the target would require a coordinated national effort involving all relevant stakeholders.

The Government is currently considering assigning responsibility for rabies control activities to the DAPH, while steps are being taken to develop a comprehensive national programme.

A training workshop was held in Negombo from July 12 to 16 with the participation of government veterinarians, representatives of veterinary associations, local government officials and animal welfare groups to prepare a national action plan for rabies elimination.

The workshop was organised by the DAPH with training support from the International Companion Animal Management (ICAM), while Battersea and Mars provided financial assistance.

Following the workshop, a basic national programme was developed to guide Sri Lanka’s efforts towards achieving rabies elimination by 2030.

The Department highlighted that a humane and coordinated approach by all stakeholders is essential to successfully eradicate rabies from the country.

title: Criminal record or false info could permanently block US entry: Embassy - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The U.S. Embassy in Colombo has warned visa applicants that criminal convictions and false information provided during the application process could lead to permanent restrictions on entering the United States.

In a public notice, the Embassy said even minor criminal offences could result in visa refusals, while consular officers have access to applicants’ criminal background information and may identify previous violations or arrests.

The Embassy urged applicants to provide truthful information in their visa applications and during interviews, warning that misrepresentations or lies could result in a ban on future travel to the United States.

“Criminal convictions can permanently bar you from entering the United States. Even minor offenses can trigger visa denials,” the Embassy stated, adding that honesty throughout the visa process is essential.

title: Tunnel collapse in India kills 12 workers - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - At least 12 workers were killed after a portion of an under-construction tunnel collapsed following a gas explosion in India's north-eastern Sikkim state, officials said.

Rescue operations are continuing to locate 13 others who are reported to be trapped in the tunnel since Monday's collapse.

The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) said the incident happened about 1.5km (0.9 miles) inside the tunnel.

The under-construction tunnel, designed to carry water from the nearby Teesta River to a hydropower plant's turbines, is part of a larger project in the Himalayan state being developed by the state-owned National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).

The accident happened "after [a] sudden burst of suspected methane gas trapped/embedded inside the rocks which led to [an] explosion generating dense fumes and toxic gases", NHPC said in a statement.

In a separate statement, the Sikkim government said the accident was caused by "methane gas combustion".

Methane is a naturally occurring gas that can sometimes be trapped underground. If tunnelling releases it into a confined space and it comes into contact with a spark or another ignition source, it can ignite or explode, a government official said.

There were 27 people working in different sections inside the tunnel - of which two managed to escape after the explosion and 25 were trapped.

"Of the 25 people who were trapped, we have recovered 12 bodies so far, and teams are working to locate the 13 other men," Superintendent of Police Sonam D Bhutia told the BBC on Wednesday morning.

The police say they have identified seven victims. One of them is from Sikkim, while others are migrants from West Bengal, Uttarakhand and Assam states.

Officials say their cause of death will be ascertained after a post-mortem examination.

The ongoing search-and-rescue operation is focused on a specific 200-metre zone where the remaining people are likely to be located, NDRF officer Mohsen Shahedi told ANI news agency.

Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang has set up a special investigation team in connection with the incident.

"We have engaged a team of experts to find out what exactly happened and how. We will take action on the basis of the findings," Tamang told reporters.

title: Tokyo urges men to wear shorts to work, but some women say it’s ’leg hair harassment’ - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - As temperatures rise this summer, Japanese men are baring more leg at work than ever before.

The Tokyo Metropolitan Government is pushing company employees to ditch their usual suit and tie for more casual attire, featuring t-shirts, trainers - and shorts.

Tokyo Governor Yuriko Koike introduced "Tokyo Cool Biz" in April, hoping to expand on her signature cool down initiative which has now become a widely recognised annual summer tradition.

Almost four months in, the newly allowed shorts in the office policy is getting mixed reviews.

Some commentators enjoy the relaxed rules, helping them work more comfortably. Others say the policy is unfair to women. Although not an official rule and more about etiquette, women are often still expected to wear tights when their work attire exposes their legs in a traditional Japanese office environment.

And a few women describe the experience of "leg hair harassment" or a term coined online as "sunehara", referring to the discomfort of being forced to see their colleague's leg hair.

"We want to give people more options in the severe heat, not tell them what to wear. There should be no issue as long as the work attire is not offensive to anyone," Tokyo Metropolitan Government environmental official Noboru Watanabe told the BBC.

A June survey by Gorilla Clinic found 53.5% opposed wearing shorts to work in the summer while 46.5% were in favour of the new recommendation.

For those against shorts in the office the main reason, for both genders, was the concern over body shape and body hair. The clinic says women significantly outnumbered men in their response, indicating that women may be more resistant to seeing a male colleague's bare legs.

In recent years more Japanese workers, notably those working at startups and tech companies, have started wearing casual clothes. But this year, the Tokyo government recommendation has made it more socially acceptable. Still, some men have been feeling self-conscious about their leg hair.

Akifumi Funatsu, the director of Gorilla Clinic, says he has noticed more clients coming to the clinic not just for cosmetic reasons, but as a matter of "social etiquette when wearing shorts". He thinks women believe that "men should have less leg hair", which has prompted them to seek laser hair removal so as not to offend those around them.

Koike first introduced the summer wardrobe shift as Japan's environment minister in 2005. She launched a national energy-saving campaign called "Cool Biz" to encourage company workers to opt for short-sleeve shirts.

Government leaders participated in the initiative, with then Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi often seen in public without wearing a tie or jacket, helping get the word out.

A few years later following the Tohoku earthquake and tsunami in March 2011, the government launched "Super Cool Biz" which expanded the guidelines to help reduce energy use both at work and at home.

As with other parts of the world, Japan has been experiencing record heat in recent months while grappling with soaring energy prices driven by instability in the Middle East.

Forecasters have warned of extreme heat this summer, with the Japan Meteorological Agency trying to raise public awareness by announcing the word "kokusho-bi", which means "brutally hot day" when the mercury exceeds 40C.

The latest weekly data shows seven people died in Japan from heatstroke and 4,580 people were admitted to hospitals in the seven days from 6-12 July, according to the Fire and Disaster Management Agency.

Besides staying hydrated and turning on the air conditioning, some of the most basic actions repeatedly encouraged by government officials, residents have turned to new products and gadgets to beat the heat.

Items such as clothes with built-in fans, disposable wet-towels, UV and heat blocking umbrellas, and portable handheld fans have been popular and sold in shops nationwide.

Experts from the Japan Academic Network for Disaster Reduction are stressing the need for heat acclimatisation as it takes several weeks for the body to adapt to high temperatures.

They say the key is to start preparing for hot weather and taking measures to prevent heatstroke during the country's rainy season, before the full summer heat arrives.

Japan also faces high humidity which makes it harder for sweat to evaporate, reducing the body's ability to cool itself.

title: Defence Adviser to Indian HC calls on Navy Commander - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The Defence Adviser to the High Commission of India in Colombo, Captain M Anand called on Commander of the Navy, Vice Admiral Damian Fernando at the Navy Headquarters today, 22 July 2026.

During the discussion that followed, Captain Anand conveyed his best wishes to Vice Admiral Fernando on reaching the apex of his naval career. Thereupon, they exchanged views on matters of bilateral interests and recalled the longstanding relations between the navies of two countries.

The cordial discussion came to an end with an exchange of mementoes.

title: PM reviews progress of education digitalisation programme - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has reviewed the progress of Sri Lanka’s education digitalisation programme and future initiatives aimed at strengthening digital facilities in schools.

The Prime Minister held a discussion at Parliament on July 21 with officials from the Prime Minister’s Office, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Digital Economy, GovTech, Sri Lanka Air Force, Sri Lanka Telecom, Dialog and other institutions to assess the ongoing digitalisation efforts.

The discussion focused on providing the required digital infrastructure to support the new education reforms introduced by the government. Under the guidance of Prime Minister’s Secretary Pradeep Saputhanthree and a specially appointed task force, several projects have been implemented over the past year, including the installation of digital infrastructure in schools, provision of smart boards, internet facilities and computers.

Officials informed the meeting that the Human Resource Management (HRM) module of the National Education Management Information System (NEMIS), developed with technical assistance from the Sri Lanka Air Force, has been fully completed in four provinces. The remaining five provinces are expected to be included within the next three months.

The NEMIS system will be used for teacher transfers in the future, and the process has already commenced in the Sabaragamuwa and Western provinces. The Human Resource Management module will also be updated continuously with new data.

The progress of providing internet facilities to schools through fibre technology was also reviewed. It was decided to complete the fibre connectivity programme by December 31, while wireless or satellite technology will be considered for schools where fibre connections are not practically feasible.

The Education Ministry Secretary has been instructed to evaluate competitive proposals from service providers and take necessary action regarding connectivity solutions.

The meeting also discussed future plans, including the full implementation of the Learning Management System (LMS) and NEMIS platforms, connecting all schools to these systems, upgrading the e-Thaksalawa online learning platform, and signing an agreement between the Ministry of Education and GovTech for further digital transformation of the education sector.

Minister of Children and Women’s Affairs Saroja Savitri Paulraj, Deputy Minister of Digital Economic Affairs Eranga Weeraratne, Deputy Minister of Education Dr. Madhura Seneviratne, Deputy Minister of Mass Media Dr. Kaushalya Ariyaratne, government officials and senior ministry officials also participated in the discussion.

title: Pakistan seeks $10 billion fund from US after mediating Iran talks, source says - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Reuters - Pakistan has asked the United States for a $10 billion exchange stabilization facility, according to a source briefed on the matter, which, if approved, could provide a lifeline for the cash-strapped South Asian economy.

The request, which is being reported for the first time, follows Pakistan's role in brokering talks over the Iran war, which raised its diplomatic profile and ‌stirred hopes that it could seek economic gains from Washington and other partners.

In the request to U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Islamabad is seeking a Bilateral Exchange Stabilization Support Facility between the U.S. and the Pakistani government worth $10 billion with maturity of up to five years.

The facility, if agreed to, would bolster Pakistan's reserves, ease pressure on the rupee and reduce its reliance on multilateral financing, even as Islamabad undertakes tighter fiscal and monetary policies in line with its International Monetary Fund program.

The U.S. Treasury declined to comment on the reported request.

Pakistan's finance ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment outside of Asia business hours

Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met with Bessent in Washington on Tuesday and said he had raised the vulnerability of the ⁠country's economy to regional geopolitical developments, the ministry said in a statement that did not mention the request.

"Senator Aurangzeb sought greater U.S. support for Pakistan’s road to market, underpinned by improved access to international capital markets, higher foreign exchange reserves, and enhanced sovereign credit ratings," it said, adding that both sides reaffirmed their commitment to deepening bilateral economic cooperation, promoting greater U.S. investment, and advancing strategic projects.

Pakistan remains under $7 billion IMF discipline that has required politically unpopular tax increases, spending restraint and reforms.

Exchange stabilization facilities are rare U.S. Treasury backstops, usually routed via the Exchange Stabilization Fund, that provide dollars, swaps or guarantees to support reserves and steady currencies.

These facilities are different from the permanent standing dollar swap lines that the U.S. Federal Reserve has with some major central banks and act as an international supply line of U.S. dollars to underpin financial stability.

A 2025 Argentina package was the first new foreign-government exchange stabilization facility operation since Uruguay in 2002, aside from Mexico's long-standing swap line, dating to the 1940s and now sized at $9 billion.

Pakistan narrowly avoided default in 2023 with a $3 billion IMF standby deal and later secured a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility, along with a separate $1.3 billion loan to build up its resilience to ‌climate change and ⁠natural disasters. But its reserves still depend on official financing, rollovers and deposits from China and Saudi Arabia.

That leaves Islamabad exposed to shifts in bilateral support and IMF disbursement delays. That vulnerability was exposed in April when Pakistan repaid about $3.5 billion, one-fifth of its reserves, to the United Arab Emirates with Saudi Arabia providing $3 billion in fresh support.

Pakistan’s central bank said in January that reserves could return to near their 2021 record, reaching $20 billion by the end of 2026.

A U.S. exchange stabilization facility would carry weight as both a liquidity backstop and political signal, easing pressure on reserves and the Pakistani rupee, while reducing the South Asian country's dependence on IMF ⁠tranches and ad hoc rescues.

IMF-backed reforms have stabilized the economy at a political cost, including higher taxes, spending restraint and limited room for development or welfare spending.

Ratings agency Fitch said in April that Pakistan's adherence to its IMF program has supported the country's funding capacity, while rebuilt foreign exchange buffers provide a cushion against economic shocks from the Middle East conflict.

But deeper constraints remain. Fitch cautioned that rising energy costs and potential supply disruptions could sharply ⁠erode the country's foreign exchange reserves.

Foreign investment in Pakistan has remained thin, deterred by recurring external crises, policy uncertainty, security risks, past profit-repatriation curbs and a narrow export base, while the country's credit rating remains deep in speculative-grade territory, keeping borrowing costs high and market access limited.

Pakistan has sought to use its ties to the Trump administration to address some of these issues, with economic cooperation that has so ⁠far spanned crypto, real estate and mining.

Pakistan has signed a stablecoin agreement for cross-border payments with an affiliate of World Liberty Financial, the main crypto business of President Donald Trump's family. It has also pursued a memorandum of understanding to redevelop the closed Pakistan International Airlines-owned Roosevelt Hotel in New York with the U.S. government, and courted U.S. mining investment, including in Reko Diq, where the U.S. Export-Import Bank has announced $1.25 billion in financing.

(1 Pakistani rupee = $0.0036)

title: Rs. 50mn worth illegal smartphones seized at Liberty Plaza - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - More than 300 illegally imported high-end smartphones, including the latest Apple iPhone models, with an estimated value of around Rs. 50 million have been seized during a raid at a shop in Colombo’s Liberty Plaza.

Police said the operation was carried out by the Walana Anti-Vice Squad.

Police also arrested a suspect in connection with the alleged illegal sale of the devices.

title: India opposition leader Gandhi freed after detention at student-led protest
summary: Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi has been released after he was detained during growing protests over the education system.

title: Ministry of Transport, Highways gets new Secretary - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Eng. (Dr.) Asiri Karunawardena as the new Secretary to the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development, the President’s Media Division said.

The letter of appointment was presented to him this afternoon (22) at the Presidential Secretariat by the Secretary to the President, Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake.

Prior to this appointment, Eng. (Dr.) Asiri Karunawardena served as the Director General of the National Building Research Organisation (NBRO).

title: DNA tests underway to confirm identities of victims in Homagama factory fire - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Authorities have commenced DNA testing to officially confirm the identities of five employees who died in a major fire at a helmet manufacturing factory in the Katuwana Industrial Estate, Homagama.

The five victims were killed after the fire broke out at the factory yesterday while around 80 employees were inside the premises. The victims were trapped on the upper floor of the building and died due to severe burn injuries.

The deceased have been identified as Sachith Dilshan, Dilip Dilanka, Sahan Udara, Mario Edward, and B. Damayanthi. However, due to the extent of the burns, authorities have initiated DNA testing to confirm their identities.

Relatives of the deceased visited the Homagama Base Hospital to provide DNA samples required for the identification process.

The Homagama Police have informed the Homagama Magistrate’s Court regarding the incident, while investigations into the cause of the fire are underway.

title: Largest marine plastic waste stock sent for recycling after MSC ELSA 3 spill - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - The largest quantity of marine plastic waste collected following the MSC ELSA 3 maritime incident has been officially cleared for recycling, marking a major milestone in Sri Lanka's coastal clean-up efforts, Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody said.

Speaking at a special awareness programme held today at Sethapola, Puttalam, Jayakody said the government remains fully committed to implementing environmental policies to protect Sri Lanka's marine ecosystem.

The event marked the official transfer of plastic waste and plastic nurdles collected over the past year at the Central Waste Storage Facility in Sethapola for recycling. The waste was gathered during coastal clean-up operations led by the Marine Environment Protection Authority (MEPA) after the Liberian-flagged cargo vessel MSC ELSA 3 met with an accident.

The programme was attended by MEPA Chairman Dr. Samantha Gunasekara, General Manager Jagath Gunasekara and representatives of MSC Shipping Company, Interocean, Colombo Logistics and the P&I Club. Agreements relating to the recycling process were exchanged, while MSC Lanka (Pvt) Ltd also presented an interim compensation cheque to MEPA.

According to MEPA, the clean-up operation removed not only plastic nurdles spilled from the vessel but also decades of accumulated marine plastic waste from coastal areas stretching from Jaffna and the northern islands to Mannar, Puttalam and the southern coastline.

Under an agreement with MSC Shipping Company, all costs associated with the clean-up and waste management operation are being borne by the company, allowing the project to proceed without any financial burden on the Sri Lankan government.

The vessel, which sank in May 2025, was carrying 643 containers, including 13 containing hazardous chemicals and 66 carrying plastic nurdles, along with approximately 452 metric tonnes of fuel.

MEPA said shoreline clean-up operations began on June 13, 2025, with the support of the Tri-Forces and the Sri Lanka Coast Guard under the National Oil and Chemical Spill Contingency Plan.

Deputy Minister Jayakody said the programme reflects the government's continued efforts to strengthen marine pollution control and safeguard the country's coastal environment.

title: Date fixed for no-confidence motion debate against Justice Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Yohan Perera and Ajith Siriwardana

Colombo, July 22 (Daily Mirror) - Parliament will debate the no-confidence motion against Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara on Friday, the Parliament Media Unit said.

The motion primarily accuses Minister Nanayakkara of failing to prevent the recent violent clash at Negombo Prison.

title: Trump wants to nominate FIFA chief for UN secretary-general: Report - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
AA - US President Donald Trump wants FIFA President Gianni Infantino to be the next secretary-general of the UN, the New York Post reported Tuesday.

Citing a source close to Trump, the Post reported that the president believes that Infantino “is respected by everyone around the world, and recognizes he has a special ability to bring people together."

Infantino, 56, developed close ties with Trump during this year’s World Cup, with the Swiss-born FIFA president making repeated efforts to court the US leader, including presenting him with FIFA’s inaugural Peace Prize in December, the report said.

A successor to current UN chief Antonio Guterres will serve a five-year term beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, the secretary-general is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council.

To obtain the post, Infantino would first need the backing of the 15-member Security Council, where any of the five permanent members can exercise a veto, before winning approval from the General Assembly.

Trump has repeatedly criticized what he sees as the UN's failure to play a more active role in resolving major global conflicts. Last year, he established a US-led Board of Peace, prompting speculation that he was creating an alternative to the UN as his administration pursued peace agreements, including between Israel and the Palestinian group Hamas. Trump denied those claims.

Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has sharply reduced US funding for the UN and withdrawn the US from several UN-affiliated organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO).
